inputs_detail.derivation: Alpha Vantage mean of 29 analysts (range $8.28-10.94), up from $8.80 90 days ago; replaces my round-1 back-derived $9.00.

Aggregator consensus is ~$11.19 (+22%). Goldman's hyperscaler capex path (+54% in 2027, +12% in 2028, confirmed by two independent reports of the Goldman note) means Vertiv's 2028 revenue growth, which lags capex by roughly 2-4 quarters, decelerates late in the year; I shade FY28 to +20% on $9.16 = ~$11.00.

VRT is at 26.6x FY27 today, level with Eaton (~26.8x) and nVent (~24.8x), so no peer-convergence discount is warranted. But Goldman notes the median AI-infrastructure stock has already de-rated from 32x to 22x forward since April 2026, and the Fed hiked in September 2026 with the 10-year near 4.8-5%. By the horizon, capex growth is heading to ~12% (second derivative negative), the base-rate setting for multiple compression in capital-equipment suppliers. I pick 24x, between the 22x AI-infra median and the 25-27x electrical peers.

bear.story: The capex second derivative turns sharply negative: Goldman's own path has hyperscaler capex growth falling from ~100% to 54% to 12%. The Texas permit freeze (TCEQ since 2026-09-21, ERCOT audit of ~300 projects due Dec 2026) outlasts the audit, as moratoria did in Singapore (3 years) and Ireland (~4 years), and orders visibility stays dark. FY27 lands ~$8.5 and the stock de-rates to ~17x, the industrial-median level, the way telecom-equipment makers de-rated in 2000-01 and VRT did in its own 2025 (-65%) and mid-2026 (-42%) drawdowns. Higher rates after the September hike add to it.

base.story: Q3 (late October) meets the top-of-guide consensus of $1.83. FY27 comes in near $9.16 and FY28 near $11, capex grows ~50% in 2027 as Goldman forecasts, and the Texas audit concludes in Dec 2026 to Q1 2027 with conditions (the Amsterdam 1-year pattern). The multiple settles at ~24x NTM EPS of ~$10.5-10.7.

bull.story: Capex beats even Goldman ($1.2T is already above the $1.1T consensus) and 2028 growth holds above 20%. 800V DC and liquid cooling add content, UIG's behind-the-meter power becomes the workaround for grid and permit bottlenecks, including the Ireland-style on-site-generation rules, and FY28 EPS heads to ~$13 at ~30x. That is a retest of the $380 high, repeating the 2025 recovery.

thesis_break_reason: At ~$150 (~16.4x FY27 consensus of $9.16 and ~14x NTM at the horizon, far below ETN ~27x, NVT ~25x and the ~22x AI-infrastructure median, and near the 52-week low of ~$134-141), the market would be pricing earnings falling, not a timing slip. That would be FY27 guidance below ~$8.5, deferred revenue falling without a revenue step-up, or permitting halts spreading beyond Texas with hyperscaler 2027 capex cut. At ~60% annualized volatility, $190-200 can happen on noise alone.

key_uncertainties: How far capex growth slows into 2028 (Goldman: +12%) and whether the multiple compresses, as in the telecom-2000 and 2025 VRT analogs, even with peers at 25-27x
Whether the Texas freeze ends with the December ERCOT audit (Amsterdam-style ~1 year or less) or lasts much longer (Singapore 3 years, Ireland ~4 years), and whether other states copy it
No orders or backlog disclosed since Q4 2025 ($15.0B, 2.9x book-to-bill); deferred revenue ($3.63B) is the only hard proxy, and deposit-driven FCF can reverse
Rates: the Fed hiked in Sept 2026 and the 10-year is ~4.8-5%; recession odds of ~35% by end-2027 come from a thin market
reasoning: Base-rates lane, round 2. (1) I took the supervisor's corrections. FY27 EPS is now the $9.16 consensus (Alpha Vantage, 29 analysts, rising from $8.80), not my back-derived $9.00. FCF is normalized because ~70% of the 2026 guide is customer deposits (10-Q). The net-cash figure now includes interim FCF (~+$0.3B at the horizon, not -$1.45B). (2) I disagree in part with discounting the capex path. The 100% -> 54% -> 12% figures are Goldman's own: a Sept-28 summary of the Goldman report and Bloomberg/Seeking Alpha headlines ($1.2T in 2027, $1.4T in 2028) confirm them independently of the X post. 'Consensus too conservative' refers to the 2027 level, not to 2028 growth. So the deceleration base rate stands, and the same report shows the median AI-infrastructure P/E has already fallen from 32x to 22x. That, plus the September Fed hike, is why I use 24x rather than 24.5-25x, and FY28 at $11.00 rather than $11.19. (3) Texas freeze base rate: data-center moratoria have lasted ~1 year (Amsterdam 2019-20), ~3 years (Singapore 2019-22) and ~4 years (Ireland 2021-25, lifted with on-site generation rules). Texas is tied to an audit targeted for Dec 10, 2026, so my central case is months, not years. It still adds weight to the left-middle, and the Ireland-style on-site power rules favor UIG. (4) Polymarket's end-2027 recession market (35%) has only ~$9.5k volume, so I treat it as weak evidence. It is consistent with Kalshi's ~38%. (5) Own-history base rates (large drawdowns followed by strong recoveries) remain survivor-biased and lightly weighted. The distribution is lognormal-like with sigma ~0.55-0.56 around a median of ~$248, and a slightly fatter left tail for the capex-deceleration, permitting and rates risks. Fair value is $254 (from $264), mean ~$266 on scenarios, and P(>= $244) is 0.525. The sell-side mean target of ~$338 remains evidence only.
